summary: The exact 13-page PDF gives a convincing finite-dimensional synthesis: code-based product marginals for both weights and Perron stationary laws coexist with exponentially many slow transfer modes, and density moments above/below the Boolean hypercontractive threshold distinguish the two strict gap regimes. No unresolved material mathematical objection was found. The score 5.00 means Very good on the high-ceiling Millennium research scale, not a probability or criterion average. Minor source-package/attribution revisions are recommended for a working-paper presentation; this is not editorial acceptance. Exact backend and isolation are unverified, and the author owns AIRR.
strengths: Theorem 1 combines positive primal and dual code distances with a finite block estimate to obtain exact linear-order labelled marginals and exponentially many slow modes.
Lemma 4 establishes the same marginals for the actual Perron stationary law without identifying it with the weighting law.
Proposition 5 computes the full parity transfer spectrum and separates it from the predecessor's heat-bath result.
Theorem 9 gives an explicit dimension-independent gap from a supercritical finite moment, permits zero weights and avoids division by the density.
Theorem 10 supplies the entire strict subcritical range for every B>1 using antipodal product tilts and a correct two-channel Gram comparison, while retaining r>=1/B.
The manuscript explicitly limits priority, endpoint, local-dynamics and physical implications.
